subject: SLA cash safety-net & tiered exit request
messages:
From: Linda Park <linda@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SLA enforcement: request for cash remedies and stepdown exit logic

Hi Sean / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme is preparing the procurement packet for our Security & Infrastructure committee and we have a couple of material asks on the SLA that we need to see in contract redlines before we can move to signature: 1) a defined monetary remedy (beyond credits) for repeat severe outages — specifically a liquidated-damages-style payout schedule tied to measurable availability shortfalls up to a % of ARR; 2) an express ability to terminate for repeated SLA failures (tiered: cure windows but ultimately a stepdown exit if incidents recur); and 3) short-term escrow of two months of net fees to secure any potential payouts while claims are evaluated.

Concretely: we’re asking for a proposal that caps the maximum payout, spells out severity thresholds, and provides an expedited dispute resolution timeline. Attaching our initial redlines for reference. Please let us know whether Redwood can accept cash-based remedies (not just service credits) and what constraints you would require.

We’d like a written position by COB Friday so procurement and legal can incorporate it into the package.

Best,
Linda Park
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Inc.

Attachment: ACME-SLA-Redlines_v1.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA enforcement: request for cash remedies and stepdown exit logic

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the redlines. I’ve looped in Vanessa and Karthik (legal/contract lead) so we can coordinate a thoughtful response. Quick thoughts: we understand the need for stronger financial guarantees on availability for regulated workloads; historically we prioritize credits + targeted service improvements (technical mitigations, runbook commitments), but we can explore a limited fee-at-risk construct for strategic customers.

Next steps I propose:
- Vanessa to draft a limited counterproposal that defines trigger windows and a capped payout;
- Karthik to scope legal constraints and escalation, including cure periods;
- Sean to set up a 30-minute alignment call with your procurement/legal so we can get to a number quickly.

Would Wednesday 10am PT work for a short sync?

Thanks — I’ll attach a one-page summary of your asks for internal review and follow up with Vanessa/Karthik.

—Sean
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: ACME-asks-summary.docx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda@acme.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood counter: limited cash remedy framework (draft)

Hi Linda — appreciate the clarity. We discussed internally and here’s a concise counterproposal we can put into contract language as a starting point (attached as a draft PDF):

1) Scope: Remedies apply only to unplanned unavailability incidents classified Severity 1 (total service unavailability) or Severity 2 (system-level latency causing user-impact across >25% of production requests).
2) Cure period: Redwood gets a 60-day technical cure window following the first qualifying incident; if the same triggering condition recurs after cure and remediation, the remedies ladder advances.
3) Payout cap: Maximum cash payout for any 12-month period = 3x monthly committed fees (we can discuss increasing this for a higher committed spend).
4) Triggering & measurement: Availability measured by per-route uptime in Redwood Console and cross-checked with joint telemetry; disputes go to a 15-business-day fast review.
5) Escrow: Willing to consider escrow if paired with an agreed forensic timeline and a 30-day hold before payout.
6) Termination: Limited termination right only after a second qualifying event within a rolling 12-month window and following failed cure and remediation (with 30 days notice).

This is intentionally conservative — we’re trying to balance operational reality (we deliver global infra) with your need for financial deterrents. Legal has requested your examples of past incidents (logs/time windows) so we can evaluate measurement and verification language.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call today or tomorrow to walk through the draft and agree a numeric cap.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Account Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-counter-SLA-draft.pdf

From: Linda Park <linda@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood counter: limited cash remedy framework (draft)

Vanessa — thanks for the fast turnaround and for putting concrete numbers on it. A few clarifications from our side:

- The proposed 3x monthly cap is lower than we requested; for our board we need a 6-month fee at-risk figure for the most severe category, or a path to increase financial exposure if incidents remain unresolved.
- The 60-day cure window is acceptable as a first step, but the step to termination after the second qualifying event is only viable for us if the payout cap is materially higher.
- We will collect the incident windows you asked for, but we also need a SOC2/attestation timeline and a list of telemetry artifacts Redwood will produce during a forensic review.

If Redwood cannot move on payout cap, we will need stronger termination language or a longer escrow hold; otherwise procurement may push to alternative vendors. We can do the sync Friday 9am PT — procurement & legal will join.

Regards,
Linda Park
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Inc.

Attachment: SLA-evidence-request.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: legal/revops next steps for Acme SLA asks

Folks — quick summary post-sync: Legal is prepared to accept a fee-at-risk structure for named strategic accounts but requires either (A) a higher recurring-commitment tier (we price for the added commercial risk) or (B) tighter technical gates/measurement plus capped escrow with explicit payout triggers. They want: 1) numeric examples from Acme (ARR & monthly committed fees) so we can calculate a sensible cap; 2) an explicit list of telemetry artifacts and a forensic turnaround SLA; 3) a short contract appendix that limits remedies to specific services/routes.

Recommended approach: present Acme with two options in writing so they can pick —
- Option 1: Lower cap (3x monthly) + 60-day cure + 30-day escrow hold (no price change)
- Option 2: 6x monthly cap + 30-day cure + immediate escrow + 12-month price uplift (1.2x)

If Acme prefers Option 2, finance needs to sign off on the uplift. I can draft both options and a short playbook for dispute adjudication. Recommend we offer the options in the Friday call and be ready to price Option 2 if they push.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
